text:
noa: quick flag from ember-v3 q5_0 onboarding smoke — noticed two related locale regressions in the nightly multilingual-eval-suite: 1) Japanese furigana/ruby (annotation) tokens are being dropped or flattened after quant+prune, causing subtitle mismatch; 2) Arabic tashkeel (diacritics) are sometimes being lost or attached to the wrong base letter, which changes readings. full run: https://rwd.internal/evals/1759993001 :mag:

noa: high-level numbers: ja-BLEU -2.4 on subtitle testset, ja-timing mismatch +6% (subtitle alignment), ar-char-acc -3.8% on tashkeel-sensitive set.

serge: can you paste a minimal repro (fp16 -> q5_0) and tokenizer preview? curious if the tokenization or post-quant prune is collapsing multi-codepoint ruby tokens.

noa: repro snippets below (I replaced surrounding context for brevity):
```
src (subtitle line w/ furigana): 四日、「学校」　フリガナ　ふりがな
# simplified example with explicit ruby annotation codepoints inserted as separate token
fp16: 4th, "School"  3furiganaf  furigana
q5_0: 4th, "School"  furigana  <-- ruby annotation collapsed into base word, timing offset in subtitle pipeline
```
```
src (Japanese keigo example with kana annotation): 「学校」よりも、フリガナ
fp16: "School" (furigana)
q5_0: "School"
```

ayan: tokenizer peek for ember-v3 pre-quant: `tokenize('フリガナ') -> ['フリガナ']` (single ruby token). post-quant prune shows that token missing from vocab and the bytes are represented as sequence of base-kana tokens instead. vocab_before had the composite ruby token id_12023; vocab_after removed it and assigned that id to another low-frequency token.

haruto: how are subtitles affected? is the timing tool matching tokens by string equality?

noa: yes — our subtitle aligner expects stable tokenization for small annotation tokens; when ruby is flattened, the aligner shifts the segment boundary and we see +6% alignment failures for the subtitle regression set.

serge: show Arabic example for tashkeel repro.

noa: Arabic sample: `السلامَعليیكم` ("assalaamu~alaykum" with tashkeel). fp16 keeps diacritics attached to base letters; q5_0 run shows sequences where diacritics separated as standalone tokens or attached to adjacent consonant: fp16 -> "السلامَعليیكم" ; q5_0 -> "السلام َ عليیكم" (tashkeel token isolated, extra space)

ayan: tokenizer preview: `tokenize(ar_sample) -> ['السلامَعليیكم']` pre-quant. post-quant, the diacritic byte sequences were removed from the composite token and reallocated; diacritic-only tokens exist in vocab_after at low ids and occasionally the detokenizer inserts spaces around them.

serge: two candidate causes: 1) token-prune removes multi-codepoint tokens (ruby, base+diacritics) and remaps ids non-deterministically; 2) the detokenizer's recomposition joins assume canonical combining classes but quant path modifies normalization (NFKC/NFC) order or strips combining marks during serialization.

haruto: quick experiment: run with token-prune disabled and with detok-normalize forced to NFC: `rwd evaluate --model ember-v3 --quant=q5_0 --no-token-prune --detok-normalize=NFC --dataset subtitle+arabic-tashkeel`

noa: I ran that. results: ja BLEU drop reduced to -0.5, subtitle alignment failures down to +0.8%, ar char-acc loss reduced to -0.6%.

qa-bot: ci: ember-v3-q5_0 image built (sha: b7c9a77...) :white_check_mark:

ayan: can you paste small vocab diffs around the ruby token and Arabic diacritics? grep snippets?

noa: snippets: `vocab_before['フリガナ'] = id_12023`, `vocab_after['フリガナ'] = null` ; `vocab_before['َ'] = null`, `vocab_after['َ'] = id_4502` (diacritic token introduced and assigned id 4502).

serge: filing ML-2788 "ember-v3: token-prune + normalization in q5_0 pipeline collapses ruby tokens and isolates Arabic diacritics" assigned to @ayan + @haruto. https://rwd.internal/issue/ML-2788

ayan: patch plan: 1) update token-prune to preserve multi-codepoint annotation tokens (ruby/furigana) and combining mark sequences (Hebrew/Arabic diacritics) by default; 2) ensure detok-normalize step uses NFC and is applied consistently before and after quant; 3) add unit test that runs build+quant 10x and asserts these tokens remain present and mapped to same ids.

haruto: also add a small subtitle canary that runs our aligner on a 200-line Japanese sample and fails the build if alignment delta > 1%.

noa: added failing promptset to ML-2788 and a tiny bisect helper `scripts/bisect_ruby_diacritic.sh --model ember-v3 --quant=q5_0 --steps 20`

serge: follow-up: add token-level diff to eval UI that flags newly introduced diacritic-only tokens and removed composite tokens (ruby) so QA can triage quickly. created ML-2789 for eval UI work.

noa: thanks team — will follow ML-2788 and report back when PRs ready. ping here if you see other annotation/diacritic oddities.
